report:
PASS for the complete current scoped argument in continuation262/native202. I independently reconstructed all 19 proof units, the unnumbered constructions and applications, and all eight exact final notes. This verdict does not close original P05.2. Higher-dimensional all-obstacle regularization, general non-PA contact sufficiency, and arbitrary irrational-reference mixed completion remain open. The earlier whole247/196 and whole255/200 FAIL verdicts remain intact.

Only the complete A224/B225/R230 papers and their supplied clarifications were treated as grants. B225 supplies positive spanning for inherited positive balanced stars, including nonsimplicial cones and common lineality, and excludes compact positive-dimensional support only in its finite globally embedded category. R230 supplies continuous completion and unrestricted-envelope identification with the actual continuous obstacle and growth bound preserved. Neither grant supplies PA approximation or an extended operator. A224 is mathematical context; its fan-specific results are not transferred to the present plane-sum or graph constructions. Historical reviews, source hashes, build observations and finite certificates were not mathematical grants.

I opened the original [BBGS publisher PDF](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00209-021-02869-6.pdf) and checked the requested complete chain. Subdivision covers inherited, opposite-contribution and zero-weight cases. Reflected codimension-two expansions give commutation; linear-form annihilation preserves balance. The printed 3.19 commuting reference uses 3.15. I also checked the literal definitions and pertinent elementary normal/refinement, PA/PC, degree/IBP and envelope units in [BMPS v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1). Its automatic-continuity assertion and broad completion/density theorems are not imported. No delegated AR10 proof is used.

The primitive-to-unit conversion is correct. Saturation makes a basis of Nτ followed by a primitive quotient lift a basis of Nσ. Thus its perpendicular projection is (aσ/aτ)νσ/τ. The Euclidean weights aσcσ balance. Subtracting an ambient extension of the face derivative cancels tangent contributions by continuity and balancing, giving B₋f(ac)(τ)=aτD_fc(τ). The negative-source sign therefore produces the positive convex primitive divisor. This identity applies successively in every dimension, including signed and zero intermediate weights, and ends with avertex=1. Refinement, symmetry and balanced preservation consequently apply to the actual raw recursion. Local supports establish positivity at each stage. No additional factorial, ambient Alexandrov mass or polygon-area definition enters the operator.

Lemma 1 is valid in both of its stated uses. For a continuous function with local affine supports, subtracting a segment chord and considering a positive maximum makes the maximum set both closed and open: both segment directions force the supporting slope to vanish. This proves contained-segment convexity. Propagating a support along the incident endpoint segments and cancelling the barycenter proves PCC inequalities. For a PA divisor on a common carrying structure, the support agrees with the face derivative, so every weighted inward residual is nonnegative and the tangent correction cancels.

Lemma 2 establishes finite support duality without a hidden convexity theorem. Small rational generator endpoints prove s·λ≥0 whenever λ≥0 and Uλ=0. The cone R₊ᵐ+im(Uᵀ) is closed: dependent-column elimination leaves independent active columns, and finitely many inverse maps bound their coefficients on bounded sets. Nearest-point separation of an infeasible s gives λ≥0, Uλ=0 and λ·s<0. Hence nonnegative relation costs produce an affine support. These tests cover every face germ, all incident cones, duplicate assignments and both lineality signs; they are not restricted to simplicial stars. Extreme kernel rays have one-dimensional kernels on their supports, support size at most rank(U)+1, and rational generators. The finite circuit tests therefore suffice.

Lemma 3 has the essential corrected PC hypothesis. B225 gives positive spanning and a nonempty compact normalized relation section; PC gives nonnegative costs. Absence of flatness then makes the minimum cost θ strictly positive. Separating s−δ1 for 0<δ<θ gives generator residuals at least δ and a quantitative norm floor, for example δ/maxᵢ‖dᵢ‖. Opposite lineality generators give a flat relation, as required. The retained negative-slope example independently demonstrates the old defect: slopes (−1,−1) have strictly negative nonzero relation costs and no zero-cost relation, but an affine floor would require simultaneously b<−1 and b>1. The old unconditional lemma remains false.

Theorems 4–5 and Corollary 6 establish the finite-PA contact criterion in their actual scope. A finite PA envelope is PC by supremum Jensen inequalities, so Theorem 4 establishes nonnegative relation costs before using Lemma 3. At a noncontact point, a small raised affine maximum remains below the obstacle, agrees with the envelope on a strict collar and preserves growth. Supports persist at active and tie points. This auxiliary unrestricted competitor need not be rational-structure PA and receives no measure. Conversely, an actual global relative PA PC function with a flat relation and positive raw atom admits the exact norm roof. Scaling generators to rational roof-boundary endpoints preserves the barycenter and zero slope cost, forcing every printed-PC competitor below the endpoint at the center. Rational radial chords give the interior bound, and shrinking rational simplices extend it to arbitrary centers without continuity of competitors. The endpoint is genuinely PA and regularizable; artificial atoms vanish. The contact integral is exactly −Rm_v. The corollary concerns PA obstacles whose actual envelopes are finite PA, not general continuous endpoints.

The fixed-structure feasibility description includes every required constraint: shared-face affine equations, all face circuit inequalities, equality with the actual reference on every recession direction, a zero extreme-relation cost and positivity of the actual degree-d raw mass polynomial. Vertex-plus-recession decomposition proves that the recession equalities are precisely bounded difference. Saturated normals and the specified actual top weights occur in the polynomial. Literal integrality and rational constants remain additional arithmetic restrictions. Common lineality together with affine invariance gives zero top atom by a carrying structure without zero-dimensional faces and refinement compatibility; mere affinity on an isolated line does not. No bound over refinements or non-PA sufficiency is inferred.

The coupled plane-sum example is correct. Each coordinate plane is saturated and unit-balanced, including the transverse classes along their shared axis. The actual gamma=max(|x|,|y|,|z|)+|z| and f=max(|x|,|y|−1,|z|)+|z| are ambient convex literal PA restrictions, satisfy −1≤f−gamma≤0, and gamma has positive growth. On the xz plane the first cycle has weight 2 on the two horizontal rays and weight 1 on the four primitive diagonals. Their outgoing slopes 1 and 2 give raw origin mass 12. On the yz plane the central axis has weight 4, the two outward axis rays weight 2, and the four graph rays weight 1. At each p±=(0,±1,0), weights 4,2,1,1 balance and slopes 0,1,2,2 give mass 6. The central artificial origin contributes zero. Thus MA(gamma)=24δ₀ and MA(f)=12δ₀+6δp₊+6δp₋. The radius-1/4 roof has unrestricted envelope f and contact −3. Horizontal corner differences are −1/4 for gamma and f and +1/4 for the obstacle, excluding precisely the cross-times-z additive decomposition. The old endpoint remains separable and failed; it is not relabeled.

The irrational-kink warning is also valid. The displayed maximum is |x−t|+t with irrational t=√2/2, so no finite rational carrying structure supports it. Rational t_n decreasing to t give literal convex approximants with exact uniform error 2(t_n−t). This disproves finite rational-PA maximum closure, while establishing regularizability for this particular maximum.

Theorem 7 and Corollary 8 preserve their rational-reference and real-category hypotheses. Finite recession decomposition gives gamma≥aρ−b with a>0. A slower rational norm, raised near the selected rational point, is gamma-inactive near that point and gamma-active outside a compact set. Inserting C+t+δh with δ|h|≤ερ/2 and t<εr/4 gives an unchanged annular collar and the exact prescribed germ near the center. Supports cover ties, all equality walls are rational, actual bounded difference is global, and the raw atom scales by δᵈ. For a real bad jet, shared-face and PC constraints are rational linear constraints. Nonnegative costs allow selection of a rational extreme zero-cost relation. Rational approximation inside the active feasible face preserves this equation and every inequality; strict positivity of the mass polynomial persists with the actual positive real top weights unchanged. This supplies real rational-reference gluing, not literal gluing or irrational-reference maximum closure. The universal quantifier over rational refinements remains essential.

Lemma 9 has the correct primitive-length and relative signs. On a bounded one-cycle edge of primitive length L, bounded PA b,c contribute −wΔbΔc/L to ∫bD_c, symmetrically. Their slopes vanish on unbounded edges, and outgoing degree contributions cancel. Replacing mixed factors by gamma one at a time therefore preserves raw mass M. Expanding bounded-difference IBP gives the printed relative identity with its two bounded error terms. Balanced intermediate cycles may have zero weights; strict positivity is not required there.

Lemma 10 reconstructs the needed compact-test DC representation. A finite rational wall arrangement permits H₀=KΣ|L_j| with H₀ and H₀+ψ ambient convex. Scaling below the actual reference recession growth and raising the slow term strictly above gamma near the test support gives actual relative rational-affine real PA PC functions θ₀,θ₁ with θ₁−θ₀=εψ. Local descriptions cover support boundaries and ties, and the slow term is inactive at infinity. These auxiliaries may be real even when the input approximation category is literal. Rational bump nets give uniform C_c density with controlled compact supports; for a compact test supported in an open equality set, the bump scale can keep its support inside that set. No C_b density or irrational-reference maximum closure is used.

Theorem 11 independently establishes both material uniformity counterexamples. On the balanced literal line, A_n=|x−2n| and B_n=|x−2n−1/(8n)| have integral slopes, rational carrying positions and constants, relative norms 2n and 2n+1/(8n), and raw measures 2δ at their respective kinks. Their distance is 1/(8n). The single fixed C_b test sin(πx²) separates their evaluations by 2cos(π/(64n²))→2. For the real averaged alternating shifts, consecutive pairs give disjoint trapezoidal differences of height 2 before division by n, so the distance is exactly 2/n. The raw atoms have weight 2/n and total mass 2. The fixed eight-periodic test has sup norm 1/4, Lipschitz constant 1/2 and evaluation difference exactly 1. Both averaged relative norms are 2n−3/2. These examples disprove the old global weak and real BL uniform-continuity guarantees, while their diverging relative bounds leave ordinary continuity consistent.

Lemma 12 supplies the complete positive-functional Radon antecedent. Open-set suprema and compact partitions give countable subadditivity; disjoint open sets give additivity. The outer construction is additive on separated sets. Alternating dyadic distance shells have summable outer masses, which establishes closed-set measurability and hence Borel measurability. Compact cutoffs give inner regularity on open sets, the outer construction gives outer regularity, and finite compact exhaustion gives the remaining regularity. Range-step upper and lower sums identify the integral of every nonnegative compact continuous function with the functional; positive and negative parts give the signed assertion. Open-set values determine uniqueness. No broad representation or completion theorem is imported in place of these arguments.

Theorem 13 constructs the operator only on the actual uniform/decreasing relative PAPC completion, separately in each coefficient category, for the same rational-affine positive-growth reference. Telescoping, Lemma 9 and Lemma 10 give |∫ψ(MA(a)−MA(b))|≤(2M/εψ)Σᵢ‖aᵢ−bᵢ‖∞. This compact-test constant is independent of relative bounds. Controlled-support density therefore gives Cauchy C_c evaluations and a positive Radon limit. For one fixed rational c, H=gamma+c≥0 is proper, J=∫H MA(gamma) is finite, and q_j=max(gamma−j,−c) is actual rational PA PC. The relative identity bounds ∫min(H,j) MA(a) by 2dDM+J whenever the finite tuple has relative bound D. Monotone truncation gives height moments and tails. Every particular uniformly convergent approximation family has a common D, so compact cutoffs prove no mass escape, exact limiting mass M and convergence against all C_b tests. Comparing arbitrary approximations proves sequence independence.

The fixed-family quantifier and exact constant are established, not merely asserted for one sequence. For every completed tuple with maxᵢ‖fᵢ−gamma‖∞≤C, choose approximations with bounds C+o(1), pass compact height tests and then increase the truncation. This gives ∫H MA(f)≤K_C=2dCM+J for every tuple in the entire fixed-C family, and MA(f){H>T}≤K_C/T. Compact-test approximation proves global vague uniform continuity. Compact cutoffs plus these common tails prove weak C_b uniform continuity only on each fixed-C family. A finite spatial mesh and value quantization give finite BL test nets on the compact cutoff support, establishing BL uniform continuity on the same family. A radius-one neighborhood of any fixed tuple has a common relative bound, proving ordinary weak continuity for sequences and nets. M=0 gives the zero operator separately. Symmetry and locality pass from finite recursion through localized compact tests. Approximation errors 2⁻ⁿ and rational additions 4·2⁻ⁿ give genuinely decreasing extraction, so uniform closure equals the declared decreasing domain. Merely continuous PC functions are not thereby admitted.

Corollary 14 retains the necessary domain hypothesis. R230 gives uniform envelope convergence and a common relative bound from uniformly convergent bounded continuous obstacles. Once the actual envelopes belong to the proved completion domain, weak C_b measure convergence and uniform convergence of the bounded contact gaps pass the contact integral to the limit. This establishes stability, not missing higher-dimensional all-obstacle membership.

The non-PA quadratic construction has its own genuine operator antecedent. The even transition a is convex, the resulting F is an ambient convex restriction, −3/2≤F−gamma≤0, and its quadratic axis restriction excludes finite PA status. Dyadic chords have slopes (j+1/2)/N, initial and final half-jumps 1/(2N), interior jumps 1/N, nested decrease and exact maximal error 1/(8N²). Their maxima F_N are actual rational-affine PA_R PC functions on finite rational structures and decrease uniformly to F.

Every raw dyadic contribution is accounted for. For a reduced slope p/q, primitive graph tangent (q,p) and a determinant-one Bezout lift give first graph weight 1/q. At the initial vertex, central/outward axis weights 4 and 2 together with the two graph rays give mass 6Δ₀. At each subsequent kink, including the final half-jump, axis weights and slopes give 4Δ_j at (t_j,0). The upper graph balance uses incoming and outgoing graph weights 1/q and downward vertical weight Δ_j, giving mass Δ_j; reflection supplies lower and negative-side atoms. Remaining walls have zero weight, and straight affine first edges cancel at artificial vertices. The horizontal sheet contributes 12δ₀ and the vertical central origin zero. Since ΣΔ_j=1, raw total mass is 24. The finite moment rows also follow from the sums: y²=28+2/N² and z²=1/5+1/(3N²)−1/(30N⁴).

The compact Riemann sums, combined with sequence independence, give exactly 12δ₀ plus two parameter segments of density 4 and four parameter parabolas of density 1 on t∈[1,2]. These are parameter pushforwards, not arc-length densities. Their total mass is 24, y² moment 28 and z² moment 1/5. The common homogeneous roof germ, rational flat endpoints, radial chords and shrinking simplices prove the unrestricted envelopes F_N and F; only the origin lies in the roof, giving contact −3. Coupling persists. On the primitive y-segment [5/4,7/4], the half increments are 3/32 and 5/32 over lengths 1/4. A convex literal approximant’s midpoint integer slope is either at most zero or at least one; comparison on the corresponding half forces error at least 3/64. No literal measure is assigned to F.

Theorem 15 independently establishes the noncompact literal obstruction without balancing. A finite noncompact complex has a noncompact connected component. For rational C>gamma(x), D=max(gamma,C)−gamma is nonnegative literal PA with compact support. After pointed rational refinement, D vanishes on each unbounded affine cell: its bounded recession slope is zero, and it eventually vanishes along that ray. A cell path from positive D to the unbounded region therefore supplies a bounded positive-dimensional cell with nonzero integral gap slope. Integer norm cones globally majorize D/N and match each fractional vertex value; taking their finite minimum with D gives the actual bounded literal obstacle. Rational vertex-plus-recession decompositions, sufficiently far rational endpoints and shrinking simplices prove its exact unrestricted envelope gamma+D/N. Its noninteger primitive slope gives the printed positive midpoint quantization bound against every literal PC approximant. The excluded endpoint receives no literal operator. B225 is applied afterward only in its finite pure positive globally embedded scope.

The dimension-zero conclusion is separate and correct. On a finite rational set all PCCs are trivial, the envelope is pointwise gamma+u for every C_b obstacle, and arbitrary real values admit uniformly decreasing rational pointwise approximations. The genuine zero-fold measure is the specified weighted cycle and the contact gap is zero. Abstract compact chart spaces retain their separate continuous-competitor and finite bounded-decomposition hypotheses; they are not excluded by the global embedded noncompactness theorem.

Lemma 16 proves all required graph derivative inequalities. Rational-endpoint approximation and continuity give ordinary convexity on each edge. At a vertex, the actual strictly positive weight relation makes the weighted sum of small rational secant quotients nonnegative. Each quotient has a finite upper bound and decreases toward its derivative; positivity of every weight prevents any derivative from tending to −∞. Thus every outgoing derivative is finite. Repeating the limiting argument for every relation proves all cone costs nonnegative. Finite support duality gives vertex supports, while edge convexity gives interior supports. Conversely these supports prove all PCC inequalities. Edge convexity alone is not used as a substitute for the vertex tests.

Theorem 17 proves real regularization for the actual reference, including arbitrary irrational coefficients. On each end, bounded relative difference and convexity force the limiting derivative to equal the actual reference slope g_e>0. The bounded nonincreasing function f−g_et has a finite limit, so replacing the tail at a sufficiently large rational position by the line of slope g_e approximates uniformly from above. Rational mesh chords on bounded edges and compact end portions have monotone slopes and approximate uniformly. At both ends of every bounded edge, each outgoing chord slope dominates the true outgoing derivative, preserving every nonnegative relation inequality. Shared vertex values agree; mesh positions remain rational; coefficients may be arbitrary real; and tail slopes are exactly those of the original reference. Decreasing extraction is genuine. R230 gives continuous relative membership for every unrestricted C_b envelope, and this theorem supplies regularization before an operator is used. It proves no literal density.

Theorem 18 constructs the genuine primitive/Stieltjes completion. The finite monotone right-continuous edge derivatives define positive Stieltjes measures through secant partition sums. The vertex coefficient is Σ_e w_ed_v,e≥0. A bounded edge’s interior mass w_e(f′₋(L)−f′₊(0)) cancels its endpoint derivative contributions; each end leaves w_eg_e. Thus total mass is M=Σ_end w_eg_e=deg(gamma), with every endpoint and artificial subdivision contribution included. Compact rational PA test IBP follows from interval telescoping, derivative Riemann bounds and vertex cancellation, giving |∫ψ(Δf−Δh)|≤TV(Δψ)‖f−h‖∞. Controlled-support density proves sequence independence, raw PA agreement, locality and global vague uniform continuity.

The graph tightness argument is independent of the subsequent moment argument. For every completed f with ‖f−gamma‖∞≤C, convexity gives f′₊(T_e+R)≥g_e−2C/R. The tail outside the corresponding compact core is therefore at most (2C/R)Σ_end w_e, uniformly over the entire fixed-C family. This already proves all-C_b convergence for uniformly convergent families. For irrational gamma, q_j=max(gamma−j,−c) is only continuous at first: Theorem 17 establishes its regularizable domain before bounded-difference IBP is passed and before its measure is assigned. Passing finite IBP using the already proved bounded-test convergence yields ∫HΔf≤2CM+J for every output with bound C. There is no circular tightness or all-C_b argument. Ordinary weak continuity uses a radius-one neighborhood; weak and BL uniform continuity remain restricted to fixed-C families.

Theorem 19 proves both contact directions for all bounded continuous obstacles in the finite embedded real graph scope. For sufficiency, a short chord replacement inside a noncontact edge interval stays below the obstacle by its positive gap and small oscillation. Secant monotonicity gives convex glue, original vertex derivatives are unchanged, and growth is preserved. Maximality forces local affinity, so curvature vanishes on every open noncontact interval. At a noncontact vertex with positive atom, K_v=R₊w_v makes every nonzero relation cost positive. Lemma 16 and the corrected floor separation apply to the finite derivative vector; convexity extends the floor estimate without requiring a PA germ. A small raised affine maximum with an unchanged collar contradicts maximality. Hence the entire positive measure is supported on contact and the bounded-gap integral is zero.

For necessity, dim K_v>1 gives a rational extreme relation omitting a coordinate: a fully positive extreme would admit a nontrivial two-sided kernel perturbation. The slope germ equal to 1 on the omitted edge and 0 elsewhere is PC, flat on that relation and has actual positive mass w_e₀. A continuous slow-norm maximum and strict collar realize it relative to the actual possibly irrational gamma. This intermediate function is neither asserted rational PA nor assigned an operator. The proved graph chord construction, with first rational samples inside the linear germ, then produces an actual relative real PA function preserving the germ, flat relation and positive mass. Only at this stage is the exact PA roof applied, yielding a bounded real PA obstacle with strictly negative contact. Bivalent subdivision vertices have the single balancing ray, so the condition is subdivision invariant. Nothing is extended to abstract compact charts or higher dimensions.

All eight exact notes agree with these reconstructed scopes: n1 records the material uniformity failure; n2 the corrected finite criterion and raw conversion; n3 the coupled example and rational-reference jets; n4 the corrected completion; n5 the genuine quadratic endpoint; n6 the literal obstruction and dimension-zero branch; n7 the all-continuous real graph theorem; and n8 preserves the open original problem. Every listed support ID refers to an earlier local note. The ledger and material-change record do not introduce additional grants. Finite rows corroborate the algebra but do not replace continuum proofs. Historical byte/hash equalities and build execution were treated as supplied provenance observations, not independently recomputed certifications.

Harmless clarifications are limited to the already disclosed BBGS 3.19 reference correction, interpreting decreasing as nonincreasing where appropriate, reading divisor-support statements on a common PA carrying structure, including j=N in the final dyadic half-jump, and distinguishing yz-sheet vertex counts from the additional horizontal origin. Graph Stieltjes measures are on edge interiors; endpoint derivatives belong to the vertex coefficients. The added PC floor hypothesis, replacement of the separable endpoint and restriction of weak/BL uniform continuity are material changes, not harmless corrections. No further mathematical repair is needed for the current scoped paper. External premise/passages below are bound by exact zero-based indices; the separate task passage records grant authorization and does not count as external evidence.

passages.quote: Exactly THREE complete A224/B225/R230 papers and ALL unchanged clarifications are grants.

premises: On a Euclidean quasi-embedded polyhedral space X, open U and common carrying complex Π, BBGS2022’s negative inward-unit-normal product accepts real PA functions and real weights, commutes with restriction/subdivision, and satisfies f·(g·c)=g·(f·c) for k-weights c, k≥2. Ambient-linear annihilation characterizes Minkowski weights, which restriction, subdivision and PA products preserve, including signed/zero weights (Definitions 3.1–3.9; Propositions 3.12/3.15/3.19; Lemma 3.18).

BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1 uses finite globally embedded rational complexes, saturated tangent lattices Nσ=N∩span_R(σ−σ), rational cycle weights, primitive inward quotient normals, and continuous PA functions with integral tangent slopes and rational constants. Definitions 3.2–3.3 require rational PCC endpoints, allowing real centers and coefficients. Definition 2.31 and Definitions 4.4–4.7 use tangent-corrected d-fold primitive recursion without an additional factorial. Definition 3.23 defines uniform relative PA regularization; Definition 4.15 requires positive nonzero recession slopes. For a PA PC reference positive at infinity and continuous obstacle, Definition 6.2 uses unrestricted PC minorants bounded above by γ+O(1); Definition 6.9 assumes pair-level regularity before orthogonality.

For a quasi-embedded polyhedral space with quasi-embedding ι and an open set U, BBGS2022 Definition 5.1 permits arbitrary endpoints xi∈U, nonnegative real coefficients summing to one and ι(x)=Σν_iι(xi). PCCs additionally require faces τ containing x and σ_i containing τ, with xi∈σ_i⊂U.
